meta.title: ACCT 321 — Transaction Template Library
meta.description: Template patterns for the random transaction generator. Each template defines a transaction type with account names, debit/credit rules, amount ranges, and difficulty level. The webapp's random generator picks a template, fills in random amounts, and presents the description to the student.
generator_notes: Amounts are randomly selected within the range, stepping by the specified increment
For 'on account' templates, the generator may optionally include credit terms in the description
For merchandising sale templates, the generator produces TWO entries (revenue + COGS)
Difficulty levels: beginner (cash-only, simple), intermediate (credit, prepaids, inventory), advanced (depreciation, bad debts, notes)

meta.description: Templates for service businesses (both sole proprietorship and corporation)

beginner.description: Performed services for a client and received $[AMOUNT] cash immediately.
beginner.explanation: Cash increases (debit) and Service Revenue increases (credit). Revenue is recorded when earned, and cash is received at the same time.
Rent Expense increases (debit) and Cash decreases (credit). Rent is an operating expense of the current period.
Salaries Expense increases (debit) and Cash decreases (credit). Salaries are an operating expense.

beginner.description: Paid $[AMOUNT] cash for utilities (electricity and internet).
beginner.explanation: Utilities Expense increases (debit) and Cash decreases (credit).
Advertising Expense increases (debit) and Cash decreases (credit). Advertising is a period cost.

beginner.description: Purchased $[AMOUNT] of office supplies with cash.
beginner.explanation: Supplies (asset) increases with a debit, and Cash decreases with a credit. Supplies are not expensed until consumed.
Equipment (long-term asset) increases with a debit, and Cash decreases with a credit.

beginner.description: The owner invested $[AMOUNT] cash in the business.
beginner.explanation: Cash increases (debit) and Owner's Capital increases (credit). The owner's investment increases equity.

beginner.description: The owner withdrew $[AMOUNT] cash for personal use.
beginner.explanation: Owner's Drawings (contra-equity) increases with a debit, and Cash decreases with a credit. Drawings reduce equity but are NOT an expense.

beginner.description: Issued common stock and received $[AMOUNT] cash from investors.
beginner.explanation: Cash increases (debit) and Common Stock increases (credit). For a corporation, owner investments increase Common Stock.

beginner.description: Declared and paid $[AMOUNT] cash dividends to shareholders.
beginner.explanation: Dividends (contra-equity) increases with a debit, and Cash decreases with a credit. Dividends reduce retained earnings but are NOT an expense.

intermediate.description: Performed services for a client and billed $[AMOUNT] on account.
intermediate.explanation: Accounts Receivable increases (debit) and Service Revenue increases (credit). Revenue is earned even though cash hasn't been collected.

intermediate.description: Received $[AMOUNT] cash from a customer for services previously billed.
intermediate.explanation: Cash increases (debit) and Accounts Receivable decreases (credit). No revenue is recorded — it was recorded when the service was performed.

intermediate.description: Purchased $[AMOUNT] of office supplies on account.
intermediate.explanation: Supplies (asset) increases with a debit, and Accounts Payable (liability) increases with a credit.

intermediate.description: Paid $[AMOUNT] cash to a supplier for supplies previously purchased on account.
intermediate.explanation: Accounts Payable decreases (debit) and Cash decreases (credit). Paying a liability reduces both the obligation and cash.

intermediate.description: Received $[AMOUNT] cash from a customer for services to be performed next month.
intermediate.explanation: Cash increases (debit) and Unearned Revenue (liability) increases (credit). Revenue is NOT recorded yet — it will be recorded when services are performed.

intermediate.description: Paid $[AMOUNT] cash for a one-year insurance policy.
intermediate.explanation: Prepaid Insurance (asset) increases with a debit, and Cash decreases with a credit. The cost will be expensed over the policy period.

intermediate.description: Paid $[AMOUNT] cash for three months' rent in advance.
intermediate.explanation: Prepaid Rent (asset) increases with a debit, and Cash decreases with a credit. Rent expense will be recognized monthly as the prepaid amount expires.

intermediate.description: Performed services for a customer who had previously paid $[AMOUNT] in advance.
intermediate.explanation: Unearned Revenue (liability) decreases with a debit, and Service Revenue increases (credit). The liability is reduced as the service is performed.

intermediate.description: Purchased equipment for $[AMOUNT], paying $[AMOUNT_2] cash and signing a note payable for the balance.
intermediate.note: Compound entry — split amount between cash and note. Requires special handling in the generator.
intermediate.explanation: Equipment increases (debit) for the full purchase price. Cash decreases (credit) for the down payment, and Notes Payable increases (credit) for the financed portion.

advanced.explanation: Depreciation Expense increases (debit) and Accumulated Depreciation (contra-asset) increases (credit). Depreciation allocates the cost of a long-term asset over its useful life.
Depreciation Expense increases (debit) and Accumulated Depreciation — Buildings (contra-asset) increases (credit).

advanced.description: Recorded estimated bad debt expense of $[AMOUNT].
advanced.explanation: Bad Debt Expense increases (debit) and Allowance for Doubtful Accounts (contra-asset) increases (credit). This estimates uncollectible receivables.

analysis.equation_impact: Assets −$[AMOUNT] (via Allowance for Doubtful Accounts) = Equity −$[AMOUNT] (via Expense)

advanced.description: Wrote off a customer's account of $[AMOUNT] as uncollectible.
advanced.explanation: Allowance for Doubtful Accounts decreases (debit) and Accounts Receivable decreases (credit). The write-off reduces both the allowance and the receivable.

analysis.equation_impact: Assets −$[AMOUNT] (Accounts Receivable) + $[AMOUNT] (Allowance decrease) = No net change

advanced.description: Received $[AMOUNT] cash for interest earned on a note receivable.
advanced.explanation: Cash increases (debit) and Interest Revenue increases (credit). Interest revenue is earned from lending activities.

advanced.description: Paid $[AMOUNT] cash for interest on a note payable.
advanced.explanation: Interest Expense increases (debit) and Cash decreases (credit). Interest is the cost of borrowing.

meta.description: Templates for merchandising businesses using perpetual inventory system

intermediate.description: Purchased $[AMOUNT] of merchandise inventory for cash.
intermediate.explanation: Inventory (asset) increases with a debit, and Cash decreases with a credit. Under perpetual inventory, the Inventory account is updated immediately.

intermediate.description: Purchased $[AMOUNT] of merchandise inventory on account, terms 2/10, n/30.
intermediate.explanation: Inventory increases (debit) and Accounts Payable increases (credit). The terms offer a 2% discount if paid within 10 days.

intermediate.description: Paid $[AMOUNT] cash to a supplier for inventory previously purchased on account.
intermediate.explanation: Accounts Payable decreases (debit) and Cash decreases (credit). Payment reduces both the liability and cash.

intermediate.description: Returned defective inventory costing $[AMOUNT] to the supplier.
intermediate.explanation: Accounts Payable decreases (debit) and Inventory decreases (credit). Returning inventory reduces both the liability and the asset.

intermediate.description: Paid $[AMOUNT] cash for freight charges on inventory purchased (FOB shipping point).
intermediate.explanation: Under FOB shipping point, the buyer pays freight. Freight costs are added to Inventory because they are a cost of acquiring the goods.

intermediate.description: Sold merchandise inventory costing $[AMOUNT_2] to a customer for $[AMOUNT] cash.
intermediate.note: Generates TWO entries. Amount 1 = selling price (Cash/Sales Revenue). Amount 2 = cost (COGS/Inventory). Amount 2 should be ≤ Amount 1.
intermediate.explanation: Two entries are required: (1) Cash increases and Sales Revenue increases for the selling price. (2) Cost of Goods Sold increases and Inventory decreases for the cost. This matches the expense to the revenue.

intermediate.description: Sold merchandise inventory costing $[AMOUNT_2] to a customer for $[AMOUNT] on account, terms 2/10, n/30.
intermediate.note: Generates TWO entries. Same pattern as cash sale but uses Accounts Receivable instead of Cash.
intermediate.explanation: Two entries: (1) Accounts Receivable increases and Sales Revenue increases for the selling price. (2) Cost of Goods Sold increases and Inventory decreases for the cost.

intermediate.description: Received $[AMOUNT] cash from a customer for merchandise previously sold on account.
intermediate.explanation: Cash increases (debit) and Accounts Receivable decreases (credit). No revenue is recorded — it was recorded at the time of sale.

intermediate.description: Sold merchandise to a customer for $[AMOUNT] cash. (Record revenue only.)
intermediate.note: Simplified version — revenue entry only. Use when COGS is taught separately.
intermediate.explanation: Cash increases (debit) and Sales Revenue increases (credit). This records only the revenue side of the sale.

intermediate.description: Sold merchandise to a customer for $[AMOUNT] on account. (Record revenue only.)
intermediate.explanation: Accounts Receivable increases (debit) and Sales Revenue increases (credit). This records only the revenue side.

intermediate.description: Paid $[AMOUNT] to a supplier within the discount period. Original purchase was $[AMOUNT_2]. The 2% discount is $[AMOUNT_3].
intermediate.note: Compound entry. Accounts Payable debited for full amount. Cash credited for discounted payment. Inventory credited for discount amount.
intermediate.explanation: Accounts Payable is reduced by the full amount (debit). Cash is credited for the actual payment, and Inventory is credited for the discount. The discount reduces the cost of inventory.

intermediate.description: Received $[AMOUNT] from a customer within the discount period. Original sale was $[AMOUNT_2]. The 2% discount is $[AMOUNT_3].
intermediate.note: Compound entry. Cash debited for discounted amount. Sales Discounts debited for discount. Accounts Receivable credited for full amount.
intermediate.explanation: Cash increases by the discounted amount (debit). Sales Discounts (contra-revenue) increases by the discount amount (debit). Accounts Receivable is reduced by the full amount (credit).

advanced.description: Recorded cost of goods sold of $[AMOUNT] for merchandise sold during the period.
advanced.explanation: Cost of Goods Sold increases (debit) and Inventory decreases (credit). This records the expense of inventory that has been sold.

advanced.description: Recorded inventory shrinkage of $[AMOUNT] after a physical count.
advanced.explanation: Inventory shrinkage (loss from theft, damage, or error) is recorded as an increase to Cost of Goods Sold and a decrease to Inventory.
